title: Debugger tooltip resolves member variables from the current script instead of the inspected object
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in : v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f], v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8], v4.0.stable.official [92bee43ad] ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) ### Issue description When execution is paused on a breakpoint, hovering an expression that accesses an object's member variable (e.g. `foo.bar`) may display the value of a member variable with the same name in the current script instead of the value stored in the inspected object. The program executes correctly and direct property access returns the expected value. The issue appears to be limited to the debugger tooltip. For example, given: ```gdscript extends Node2D var bar func _ready(): bar = "scene variable" var foo = Foo.new() foo.bar = "foo variable" print(bar) print(foo.bar) # prints "foo variable" ``` Hovering over `foo.bar` shows `scene variable` instead of `foo variable` The print() output and the Evaluator are correct, so the bug appears to affect only expression evaluation in the tooltip. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a scene with a script containing: ```gdscript extends Node2D var bar func _ready(): bar = "scene variable" var foo = Foo.new() foo.bar = "foo variable" print(bar) print(foo.bar) ``` where Foo is: ```gdscript class_name Foo var bar ``` 2. Place a breakpoint after assigning `foo.bar`. 3. Run the scene. 4. When execution stops, hover the mouse over `foo.bar`. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
